correctness.rationale: The proof reduces post-transfer safety to the exact domination criterion for complete multipartite supports. The cases of at least three supported parts, exactly two supported parts, and one supported part are exhaustive. In the two-part case, a zero in one supported part fails exactly when the opposite part has total weight one and at least two zeros remain in the attacked part. In the one-part case, the supported part must be fully positive, with only the stated singleton exception. The polynomial is inclusion-exclusion over these exact profile conditions. Independent exhaustive replay checks every labeling of every ordered part profile through total order 8 and matches both membership and coefficients.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification of every feasible one-move weak Roman guard allocation on the basic complete multipartite family, not merely another minimum-number computation. The enumerator refines the known scalar parameter into all weights, exposes the exact two-support obstruction, and can support counting, random-allocation, and reliability questions. The classification is compact, self-contained, and structurally tied to complete multipartite domination rather than to an arbitrary finite slice.
